title: Paumanack / Eastern Long Island
summary: Paumanack is a broad Indigenous placename documented for Eastern Long Island, not a single village, creek, neck, or pond. Its marker is a representative regional label rather than a boundary.
address_label: Eastern Long Island (representative map label near Riverhead / Peconic)
map_geometry_source: Representative regional label point near the Riverhead/Peconic gateway; Paumanack is broader than a single coordinate.
why_this_matters: Paumanack names Eastern Long Island at a regional scale and keeps Indigenous political and geographic relationships visible beyond modern town boundaries. The representative marker invites visitors to read the linked records without reducing a broad homeland to one exact coordinate.
introduction_content: Paumanack, also written Pommanock and in several other forms, is a broad name for Eastern Long Island associated in colonial records with eastern Long Island sachemship and territory.
history_content: Broader Eastern Long Island scope, sachem-title language, and later interpretations are brought together here. Time-specific source details are handled through Timeline Entries and reference icons.
translation_content: The name has been interpreted as land of tribute or contributing land. Recorded forms include Pommanocc, Pamunke, Pammanach, Pawmanuck, Pammanake, Paumanuck, Paumanacke, Pamanack, Pommanock, and Paumanhacky. These historical interpretations should not be treated as a definitive modern-language translation.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is placed near the Riverhead and Peconic gateway to the East End as a regional label. It does not claim that Paumanack was a single point or define a territorial boundary.
